clauses.title: The Pensions Regulator (TPR) - Code of Practice (DC) / Governance and Administration
clauses.body: Trustees should maintain effective governance and administration, including data quality controls, record-keeping processes, and oversight of service providers. Evidence of controls and remediation actions should be retained and made available for audit.

clauses.title: TPR - Common and Conditional Data
clauses.body: Trustees should understand and monitor common and conditional data requirements, including member identifiers, dates, status and benefit-related fields. Data completeness and accuracy should be assessed periodically and after significant events such as system migrations.

clauses.title: Guaranteed Minimum Pension equalisation (GMPe) - Legal context and audit trail expectations
clauses.body: GMP equalisation projects require documented methodology, clear mapping from source data to calculations, and a defensible audit trail for decisions. Inputs, assumptions and calculation pathways should be recorded for trustee and auditor review.

clauses.title: GMPe - Minimum input data and reconciliation controls
clauses.body: Member identifiers, service dates, contracted-out history and benefit splits should be validated for completeness and consistency prior to running equalisation calculations. Exceptions should be queued for review and remediation.

clauses.title: Pensions Act - Records, reporting and trustee responsibility (general)
clauses.body: Trustees are responsible for the proper administration of the scheme. Systems and processes supporting scheme administration should be controlled, evidence-based and capable of producing accurate reporting.

clauses.title: TPR - Cyber controls and operational resilience (pensions)
clauses.body: Trustees should consider cyber risk and operational resilience, including access controls, monitoring, audit logging, and secure handling of member data. Data minimisation and segmentation support resilience and compliance.
